subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I know you have been __really busy__ with your work, but can you just give me a few minutes?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"snowed under"** means to be overwhelmed with a large amount of work or tasks. (काम में दबा हुआ)

 
 
• **Example: **She has been **snowed under** with work ever since she got promoted.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **through thick and thin** (हर हाल में साथ देना): Refers to supporting someone in both good and bad times.

 
 
• **Example:** They remained friends through thick and thin.
 
 
 
• **jumped on the bandwagon** (प्रचलित चीज़ में शामिल हो जाना): Means to join others in doing something that is currently popular or fashionable.
 
 
• **Example: **He jumped on the bandwagon and started investing in cryptocurrency.
 
 
 
• **on cloud nine** (बेहद खुश होना): Refers to being extremely happy or elated.
 
 
• **Example:** She was on cloud nine after winning the lottery.
